prompts.text: What makes a friendship feel different after people have worked through a disagreement together?
Describe the first time a friend surprised you by understanding a difficult choice.
Learn about a friend's earliest ambition or how their priorities have changed since then?
One friend sees an old disagreement as resolved while the other still has questions. How could they start again?
A friendship sometimes changes more through one careful conversation than years of casual contact.
Being able to disagree without an audience is an underrated skill between friends.
What does a friend do that makes it easier to tell them you've changed your mind?
Tell me about an assumption you made about someone close to you that proved inaccurate.
Two old friends realise they remember the same turning point differently. What might they ask each other?
Understand why a friend made a difficult decision or hear how they felt after it?
Which part of your upbringing most influences the way you show affection to friends?
Recall learning that a friend's household had very different rules about visiting.
Compare family traditions around welcoming guests or how relatives celebrate small achievements?
Two friends each assume the other prefers frequent phone calls. What question could clear that up?
People often bring unspoken expectations from home into adult friendships.
Differences in communication can reflect upbringing rather than a difference in commitment.
What's a childhood experience that explains something important about how you make friends now?
Describe a family saying that helped you understand a friend's reaction to an event.
A friend tells you that a gesture you consider casual is deeply significant in their family. How would you learn more?
Ask about a friend's childhood neighbourhood or the person who helped them feel included at school?
How do you recognise a friend who's growing more confident in their own decisions?
Tell me about supporting someone through an ambition that wasn't part of their original plan.
Hear about a friend's most recent change of direction or the goal they're reconsidering?
A friend accepts a job far away from everyone they know. What would you ask beyond the obvious logistics?
Encouraging a friend's growth can mean accepting changes that make your routine less convenient.
A close friend doesn't have to understand every ambition in order to respect it.
Which personal achievement of a friend changed the way you saw their abilities?
Recall a time you discovered an interest or talent a long-time friend had never mentioned.
One person in your circle begins a new course and has less free time. How should the group adapt?
Celebrate a friend's completed project or spend an afternoon learning how they made it happen?
What signals that a person wants encouragement rather than an immediate solution?
Describe a time you felt supported because someone listened without trying to fix anything.
Ask a struggling friend what kind of help they want or offer one specific practical favour?
A friend says work has become overwhelming but isn't ready to explain why. What might a respectful check-in sound like?
The kind of help someone appreciates can change with the circumstances.
Support becomes less useful when the helper insists on being indispensable.
How do you tell a friend you'd rather have company than advice?
Recall somebody recognising that you needed time before discussing a disappointment.
A friend worries they're becoming a burden by asking for support. How could the group respond without making promises it can't keep?
Bring someone a meal during a difficult week or quietly take an errand off their list?
Which values do you think matter most when friends share money or belongings?
Tell me about arranging a group purchase where expectations needed to be clarified.
Set written expectations before lending something valuable or simply agree on a return date?
A friend accidentally damages an item they borrowed. What would help both people discuss it fairly?
Money misunderstandings between friends often begin with assumptions neither person said aloud.
Discussing a budget early is a form of consideration, not a sign of mistrust.
What makes you comfortable contributing to a group expense?
Recall a friend suggesting a more affordable plan when someone else was hesitant to speak.
Someone can't contribute equally to a shared gift but wants to participate. What alternatives would you offer?
Pool money for one experience or exchange small personalised gifts among friends?
What's a sign that a friend's humour is helping you relax rather than distracting from the issue?
Describe a moment somebody's gentle joke turned an awkward meeting into an honest conversation.
Share an old funny memory during a tense week or create a lighthearted new distraction?
Someone tells a joke about an absent friend and you aren't sure they'd appreciate it. What could you ask?
People can be close for years and still have very different limits around teasing.
Knowing when to apologise for a joke matters more than explaining why it should have been funny.
How have your boundaries around friendly teasing changed since your school days?
Recall discovering that a joke you enjoyed made somebody else uncomfortable.
A group tradition began as teasing but no longer feels inclusive. How would you suggest changing it?
Keep humour spontaneous or agree on a few topics your group avoids?
Which unfamiliar perspective have you gained from a friend in a different generation?
Tell me about a friendship with someone older or younger that changed your habits.
Ask an older friend what they wish they'd understood earlier or a younger friend what surprises them about adulthood?
Two friends have opposite expectations about when to settle down. How could they explore the reasons without judging?
Age differences can be less important than the experiences friends are willing to share.
A younger friend can be a mentor in an area where an older friend lacks experience.
What's one life lesson you learned from somebody who was at a different stage of life?
Recall someone helping you navigate a situation they'd already encountered.
A group of friends spans several generations and plans a shared project. How could their different experiences help?
Trade stories about first jobs or compare the way each generation learnt to make friends?
What part of being a friend becomes harder when people live in different places?
Describe meeting an old friend after a long gap and noticing what remained familiar.
Schedule regular short calls or make occasional longer visits when possible?
Two friends keep missing each other's calls because their work hours differ. What small routine could help?
Distance often changes how friendships are maintained, not necessarily how much they matter.
A friendship shouldn't require people to be available at the same hour every day.
How do you distinguish a natural quiet period from a friendship that needs attention?
Recall receiving a thoughtful message from someone you hadn't spoken with for months.
Your friend abroad misses a milestone in person but wants to participate. What would make them feel included?
Exchange small voice recordings over time or set aside one unhurried conversation each month?
What can a person learn about a friendship from how the pair handles an unexpected change?
Tell me about a plan that fell apart and revealed something useful about your friend's character.
Reflect on what makes friendships last or talk about the people who helped you become more independent?
A friend is no longer interested in a shared hobby that brought you together. What else could sustain the connection?
Relationships often need new forms when the original reason people met is no longer central.
A friendship can become quieter and still be important to both people.
Which habit in your friendships would you like to carry into the next decade?
Recall a time you deliberately made space for someone whose life had changed.
Your circle wants to create a tradition that accommodates different budgets and schedules. What qualities should it have?
Keep one dependable annual reunion or build smaller, flexible ways to connect throughout the year?
Which friend has challenged you to be kinder in a way you hadn't expected?
Recall somebody treating a stranger with respect and inspiring you to do the same.
Discuss the everyday kindnesses you notice or the gestures people tend to overlook?
You and a friend witness somebody being excluded at an event. How might you act together?
A person's treatment of strangers can teach friends more than the way they talk about kindness.
Consistency in ordinary kindness is more revealing than occasional public generosity.
What's a compassionate quality you developed through knowing a particular friend?
Describe a time you and a friend volunteered together and learned different things from it.
A friend wants to help someone but isn't sure their offer is welcome. What question would you suggest?
Support a friend's community project by helping in person or contributing a skill remotely?
